t.t: Family care in Pakistan for overseas Pakistanis

Faizy looks after your family in Pakistan while you work abroad. Groceries, medicines, doctor visits, eldercare and NADRA paperwork, booked on WhatsApp and finished with a photo. From PKR 1,999 a month.

div.p: You are far away. Someone still has to queue at the pharmacy, sit with your father at the doctor's, chase the NADRA office. Faizy is that someone — family care in Pakistan for Pakistanis living abroad, asked for on WhatsApp and finished with a photo.
Your mother says everything is fine.
The prescription ran out eleven days ago.
Distance is not the problem. Not knowing is.

div.h2: The things you would do yourself
Three steps. No app to learn.
div.p: You already use WhatsApp all day. So do we. The portal is there when you want the detail — receipts, photos, history — not because you're forced through it.

div.h3: Tell us who to care for
div.p: Each family member gets their own FMB ID, so "the medicines for Ammi" is never ambiguous — not to us, not to the Faizy on the ground.
Send what's needed. You get a written confirmation with a reference number, then the name of the Faizy assigned to it.
A photo and an itemised receipt when it's finished. Not a promise that it happened — evidence.

div.h2: People you would trust with your mother
div.p: CNIC verified. References called. Rated after every task.
Your first three care activities are on us.

button.span: What counts as a care activity?

div.div: One task: a grocery run, a medicine collection, a doctor visit, a document errand, a visit to sit with your parents. Emergencies are never counted.
CNIC verification, references we actually call, an interview and a signed code of conduct. Every task is rated afterwards, and the rating follows the Faizy.

button.span: Do I have to be in the Gulf?

div.div: No. What matters is where your family is, not where you are. We have subscribers in Dubai and Riyadh, and just as many in London, Manchester and New York — each billed in their own currency.

div.p: No card needed to begin. Tell us who to look after, and we'll take it from there.
